notes.note: Titan rejects replace() on an array operand; the standard explicitly allows arrays (C.4.3), so the Titan warning is a tool limitation.
Titan rejects array operands of replace(); allowed per C.4.3. Record-of root type is observed by inserting at the end so the result grows beyond the array size.
Terminology issue ('value inpar'): tested with values; template inpar/repl are covered by the C.4.3-011a/013a tests.
Ambiguous; the test only checks that the template result can be used as a template (present) (assigned to a present-restricted variable and parameter), which holds under both readings.

Spec conflict: inpar is a template (present) formal parameter, which forbids AnyValueOrNone at top level, yet the rule requires inpar to contain *. The test follows the rule (passes * via an unrestricted variable); a tool applying the restriction check would raise an error instead.
Ambiguous lead-in; reading chosen: AnyValue in repl is converted to a single AnyElementOrNone when inpar is a binary string. repl is given as a typed template variable because a bare ? has no type.

Spec conflict: ifpresent at top level violates the template (present) restriction of inpar, but substr only yields ifpresent for inpar with ifpresent or AnyValueOrNone. The test uses inpar '0101'B ifpresent and observes ifpresent on the result via an optional record field.
Ambiguous; tests only alternative (a), a reference to a present-restricted template; the result is used as template (present). The present restriction itself is not directly observable.
The value restriction is observed by assigning the result to a template (value) variable and applying valueof.
Positive test: the same parameterized and in-line modified templates that are valid send arguments are accepted by encvalue. Terminology: 'send statement' read as send operation.
Hard to test without a codec: noexecution test with an encvalue/decvalue round trip; correctness of the encoding itself is not checked (the standard does not require a check).
No codec available: noexecution test that selects each of two encode attributes via dynamic_encoding; the codec actually used is not observed.

No codec available: noexecution test that applies dynamic_encoding to a type with nested fields that carry multiple encode attributes (the recursive selection of clause 27.9); the selection is not observed.
Uses an encode attribute naming a non-existent codec ('NoSuchCodec'), so the error is expected at run time. A tool may instead report it at build/link time.
